chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
about a man and a woman praying in one house.
So he said: “If there is between them the measure of a handspan, she may pray beside him by herself and he by himself; there is no harm.”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.مُعَاوِيَةُ بْنُ وَهْبٍ: Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb, the narrator asking the Imam عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: Can a man and a woman pray side by side in the same room?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about a man and a woman praying in the same place. It states that if there is a handspan of space between them, their praying side by side individually is permitted and there is no harm in it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.746 - Muawiya ibn Wahb asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)
about a man and a woman praying in the same room.
Imam (as) said: "If there is a space of about a handspan (shibr) between them, She may pray beside him alone and he alone; there is no harm."
